headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Windsurf can write/modify shared workspace state while ai-engineering-hub is a non-runnable docs-only repo, making direct pairwise harm limited but real if they share files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf has clipboard and workspace-file I/O plus MCP/tool use, so if it ingests content from ai-engineering-hub via shared files or copy-paste, prompt-like instructions could be misread. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and non-runnable, so the pathway is indirect, but the shared-file/clipboard bridge is plausible.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into Windsurf prompts or workspace files
IF Windsurf parses repository text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based prompt ingestion
Keep the repo in a read-only folder
Add a manual review step before acting on file text
Use separate workspaces for docs and coding tasks

B_data_leakage.rationale: ai-engineering-hub touches no data classes and has no write or network surface, while Windsurf can read workspace files and has broad egress. With no sensitive data shown in either profile, leakage risk is limited unless the shared workspace contains secrets or open files.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Windsurf's workspace
IF Windsurf sends open-file contents to external model services
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the shared workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive repo clone
Turn off auto-upload of file contents where possible
Review open files before invoking the agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model shares state via local filesystem. ai-engineering-hub is a repo artifact that could be colocated with Windsurf workspaces, so overlapping writes can race even though the first profile itself is non-runnable. Uncertainty about actual co-location pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local directory
IF Windsurf auto-commits or edits files while the repo is being updated
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
Enable explicit command approval only

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf's Cascade loop can act on file contents and tool outputs, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub material as authoritative guidance, errors can propagate into edits or commands. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only, so the risk is inference from documentation rather than a verified execution chain, which keeps this below high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses repo text as ground truth for code changes
IF no human verification occurs before execution
mitigations: Require human review of generated actions
Cross-check claims against primary docs
Disable auto-execute
Limit the agent to draft-only mode

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency mismatch, or retention policy conflict is documented. ai-engineering-hub is open-source docs-only, while Windsurf is closed-source and may handle model-provider keys, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance breach pathway. The other agent is not cited beyond its source type because no specific regulated data flow is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Windsurf-managed files
IF organizational policy forbids closed-source tooling for the repo
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Review vendor security and retention settings
Use a policy-approved environment only
Document data handling boundaries
